stable.label: ecosystem-flip-ocean-tested
stable.note: The ecosystem remains the primary experience. A camera-local 2D FLIP/PIC water solver is now wired last, but only local deterministic tests have passed so far. CI and deployed iPhone behavior are not yet promoted.

active_experience.current_change: replace camera-near visible water motion with continuous particles transferred to/from a MAC velocity grid, pressure-projected for approximate incompressibility, then advected with FLIP/PIC blending; add an anchored ocean boundary with wave/tide forcing
simulation_changes: camera-near water is represented by persistent particles with continuous positions and velocities instead of falling-cell moves
particle velocity is transferred to a staggered MAC grid, gravity is applied, and a pressure Poisson solve reduces divergence before velocity is transferred back to particles
FLIP/PIC blending preserves more motion detail than pure PIC while retaining damping for stability
water particles collide against the authoritative V104 2D terrain material field

existing visible V104 water, refined subcell water, and surface_liquid water depth are absorbed into a per-column deferred reservoir and respawned into FLIP particles near the camera instead of being rendered as the primary water
particles leaving the active camera window are converted back into the deferred per-column reservoir rather than simply deleted when they remain inside the world

the ocean reservoir is anchored to an actual world edge rather than the screen edge and injects tracked water area plus oscillatory wave/tide momentum only when that coast is inside the active solve window
submerged creature nodes receive drag and current coupling from the solved velocity field
high solved water speed couples back into hydro_geomorph25 soil mass so moving water can erode actual terrain state
approximations: flip_ocean is a 2D camera-local free-surface FLIP/PIC approximation, not full 3D water physics
the pressure solve uses a finite Jacobi iteration count and therefore only approximately enforces incompressibility
the active liquid solve runs at about 30 Hz on mobile while rendering can run faster
offscreen/far water remains in older reservoir representations and is converted approximately by conserved 2D area when it enters the active window
the ocean boundary is an external source/sink reservoir; total closed-world mass conservation therefore does not apply while the ocean boundary is active, but source/sink area is tracked
the visible water surface is reconstructed from particle positions; it is not a level-set or VOF interface reconstruction
terrain collision is still 2D and the world depth layers are not full 3D fluid obstacles
this implementation is CPU typed-array JavaScript, not WebGPU compute yet
lava remains on the older continuous surface_liquid approximation
creature locomotion still contains legacy authored body drive and feeding still lacks stomach digestion

flip_ocean.representation: camera-local 2D FLIP/PIC incompressible free-surface liquid with staggered MAC grid pressure projection and an external ocean boundary reservoir

surface_liquid.note: Still retained as a far-field/reservoir and for current continuous lava handling; flip_ocean drains camera-near visible water from it before rendering.

active_objective: Run independent CI on flip_ocean, then exercise the deployed route on iPhone. The device check must verify that the old falling-cell water is no longer visibly dominant, ocean waves remain stable, pressure solve frame cost is acceptable, and camera panning does not teleport water because particle coordinates are re-based when the active window moves.
next_gate: CI_PASS requires both Codehood and Foundation workflows to pass from a marker-only proof branch. LIVE_TESTED and DEVICE_TESTED still require actual browser/iPhone execution afterward.
invariants: Do not call flip_ocean full 3D water physics
Do not call the private Sandcastle solver copied or reproduced
FLIP/PIC claims require particle-grid-particle transfer plus pressure projection
Ocean source/sink mass must be reported separately from closed-domain conservation
Old falling-cell water must not remain the primary visible camera-near liquid
CI_PASS does not imply LIVE_TESTED or DEVICE_TESTED
